answer: Assign each agent random work from an island of unrelated tasks, never letting it pick the cheapest, and anchor its earning weight to how well it handles what it is given. A lotus on one quiet pond proves little, but an agent that writes code one epoch and audits a stranger's data the next proves breadth no clone farm can fake cheaply. Sybils scattered across random assignments score low on most, so their weight stays near zero while genuine agents earn more on basalt-solid varied work.
